- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- When sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.00) or shows strong downward momentum, model often underestimates; increase forecast lows by 2–5%.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5–10% above recent high); apply a 1–3 day lag correction to peak forecasts.
- Mean reversion is evident in 30d forecasts: model often fails to capture downward drift after 10+ consecutive days of rising prices; adjust downward by 1–3% for 3–5 day horizons.
- Forecasts with sentiment history showing mixed or neutral (0.00–0.33) show persistent bias; apply a 1–2% downward adjustment to avoid overconfidence in mid-range predictions.
- Horizon-specific: 30d forecasts are prone to overestimating early-term volatility; reduce first 5–7 days of forecast by 1–3% if sentiment is volatile or uncertain.
